summary: Iteration 2 frontend-only retest. The previously failing WIN-flow bug is FIXED. After winning Math Quiz (easy, 100%), the time wallet correctly shows 5 and the daily-challenges pill shows '1 DONE TODAY' on Home. All other critical flows requested by E1 also work: wallet history row appears with PASSED + 5 MIN, +/- buttons move 5 min between wallet and per-app, app-locked countdown decrements every second (3s drift over 3s wait), persisted countdown drift across close/reopen is small (2s), premium pass unlocks min-challenges editor in Settings and shows clock icons in Manage, and Reset App returns to setup-password. The StateContext stateRef + write-chain refactor in iteration 1 fix-applied resolves the stale-closure race condition correctly.
action_items: (Cosmetic / non-blocking) Console emits a deprecation warning: "shadow*" style props are deprecated. Use "boxShadow". And: props.pointerEvents is deprecated. Use style.pointerEvents. These come from BrutalCard / overlays in the Brutal components and from Modal. Migrate to RN Web's modern API at some point.
critical_code_review_comments: StateContext fix is correct: using stateRef.current as the source of truth inside persist((cur)=>...) and serialising writes via writeChainRef avoids lost updates when GamePage.handleComplete awaits addWalletMinutes -> incrementDailyChallenges -> recordHistory in sequence. The write chain also makes app-locked decrementAppSeconds safe even when fired every second.
app-locked.tsx now persists every 1s (was 5s). With the write-chain serialisation this is fine — confirmed close/reopen drift is ~2s, well within tolerance.

Minor: home.tsx `wallet-minutes-text` testID is rendered twice in the DOM during route transitions (Expo Router keeps stale screens in DOM tree). Tests should use visibility filtering. Not a real bug, but be aware in future test scripts.

rca_of_issue: Iteration 1 RCA: stale-closure in useCallback actions caused sequential awaited persist() calls to clobber each other. FIX (now verified working): StateContext.tsx now keeps stateRef.current always pointing to latest state and persist() takes a (cur)=>next mutator that reads from stateRef inside a serialised writeChainRef Promise. handleComplete in app/game/[id].tsx now correctly accumulates addWalletMinutes(5) → incrementDailyChallenges() → recordHistory() into a single coherent state. App-locked decrementAppSeconds is fired every second through the same chain and the per-second persist no longer drifts (close→reopen drift was 2s in test).
